answer: Randomized Quorum Assignment. Each epoch, a verifiable randomness beacon assigns every agent to a small quorum drawn from the full population; membership weights follow a skewed shale-like distribution so most quorums are thin. An agent's action is valid only if its quorum reaches a delta threshold of distinct signatures, and quorum rosters stay sealed behind a prism of commit-reveal until the beacon fires. Because an attacker cannot precompute which peers will judge it, each sybil identity must sustain real participation across many unpredictable quorums for multiple epochs.
